sourceMode: source-built SwiftPM targets; original Package manifests retained

priorPhysicalConnection.scope: Physical iPad Guest connection and directory access; not final rendered playback acceptance

currentPhysicalConnection.scope: Current source guard: real iPad Guest directory/read/seek and rendered output for one MKV. Broader player regressions are tracked separately.

persistentReadOnlyHandle.description: Bounded read-only pread handle on the existing authenticated session. Independent serial file queue; explicit close before session disconnect. Caller retains pre/post path stat and compares server document identifier; absent identity falls back to original per-range contents API. Guest/signing/encryption policy unchanged. Manager disconnect also drains registered path-stat/fallback operations via gracefully:true. Source close cancels active range progress flags before draining. Each wire READ is capped at 1 MiB even when the negotiated server limit is larger; a larger total range checks cancellation between chunks.

disconnectLifecycle.description: Stop the socket receive loop after a completed protocol callback deliberately closes its context. Preserve TREE_DISCONNECT and LOGOFF NTSTATUS errors through the existing errno callback instead of fabricating allocation failure or success. Guest/signing/encryption and stat access remain unchanged.
disconnectLifecycle.scope: C loopback socketpair contracts are not authentication, real NAS or physical-device acceptance.

fileHandleEpoch.description: 2026-11-14, after an EXC_BAD_ACCESS in smb2_destroy_context on the owner's iPhone (build 135, an SMB film replaced 0.45 s after it opened, its read-ahead switching ranges): a client's file-handle epoch moves on, under the context's lock, whenever libsmb2 frees every file handle of the context (a disconnect's smb2_free_all_fhs, a context destroyed after a failed service or as the client goes). SMB2FileHandle records the epoch it was opened in and, under the same lock, never reads, closes or names a handle from an earlier epoch: it is said to be closed (EBADF). SMB2Client's deinit no longer says a tree disconnect of its own (the manager said one; a second one serviced the socket again from whichever thread let the client go); destroying the context still closes the socket and frees what it holds. lseek and fileId take the lock they skipped. Guest/signing/encryption, the read-only handle's queue and every request and reply are unchanged.

contextListLock.description: 2026-11-26, Vision Pro's own (V-D108), after three EXC_BAD_ACCESS in smb2_destroy_context on the owner's headset within ten minutes (as SMB2Manager.disconnectShare let a client go; in one, three contexts destroyed at once while a NAS's video stills closed their readers). libsmb2 keeps every context in one global list (active_contexts) that smb2_init_context adds to and smb2_destroy_context removes from with no lock, SMB2_LIST_REMOVE moving the list's head while it walks; AMSMB2 locked each context on its own, never the list. Every smb2_init_context and smb2_destroy_context AMSMB2 makes (a client made, a client gone, a context destroyed after a failed service) now takes one process-wide lock (SMB2Client.withContextList). libsmb2's only other walks of the list are its server's (smb2_serve_port), unused. libsmb2 is unchanged. Without the lock, 16 threads making and destroying 6,400 contexts looped forever in SMB2_LIST_REMOVE (init.c:392); with it they leave the list whole (SMBContextListTests).
